newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower, central bank steps in.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower, central bank steps in.

text.p: The won closed Tuesday's tight range trading lower as the central bank intervened in the inter-bank foreign exchange market, dealers said.

They said the Bank of Korea bought dollars at 891.10 in the morning session to siphon off ample dollar positions in the market. But they said the won/dollar market still remained long for the dollars.
The Bank of Korea does not confirm its intervention.
Dealers said exporter deals limited the dollar's rebound.
The won finished at 891.00, comparing with Monday's close of 890.90. It moved in a 891.50-890.40 range.
"Domestic corporations dominated the market," said a dealer. "We just don't know what to do because of long dollar positions and intervention fears."
Dealers forecast the won would rise to 890 level on Wednesday.
Trading volume was estimated at around $1.39 billion. Wednesday's mid-rate was expected to be fixed at 891.00 against 891.20 today.
